test_title: PYST 22: SSC MTS 2024 - English Language and Comprehension (Held On: 17 Oct, 2024 - Shift 2)
subject: english
question:
Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom.

Beat around the bush

options.text: To avoid getting to the point of an issue

solution: The correct answer is: **Option 2**. [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__** __ • The idiom **"Beat around the bush"** means to avoid getting to the point of an issue. (किसी मुद्दे पर सीधे न आना) • **Example:** Stop beating around the bush and tell me what you really think. • **"To avoid getting to the point of an issue"** means to speak or act in a roundabout manner to delay or avoid discussing the main topic. (मुख्य मुद्दे पर चर्चा करने में देरी करना या बचना) • **Example:** Instead of addressing the problem directly, he kept avoiding getting to the point of the issue. Therefore, the correct answer is: **Option 2**. [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__** Here are the other options explained along with their Hindi meanings and example sentences: • **Option 1: To speak rashly** (बिना सोचे समझे बोलना): To speak without considering the consequences. • **Example:** He often speaks rashly, which gets him into trouble. • **Option 3: To speak abusively** (गाली-गलौज करना): To use offensive or insulting language. • **Example:** He was criticized for speaking abusively to his colleagues. • **Option 4: To speak convincingly** (विश्वासपूर्वक बोलना): To speak in a manner that persuades others. • **Example:** She spoke so convincingly that everyone agreed with her plan. 32:T9af, The correct answer is** option 2.**
